title: Medical Terminology: Prefixes & Suffixes
description: Common prefixes and suffixes used in medical terms, each with an example word. Useful for health science students.
subject: medicine-health

cards.definition: Inflammation. Example: tonsillitis, inflammation of the tonsils.
Fast. Example: tachycardia, an abnormally fast heart rate.
Surgical removal. Example: appendectomy, removal of the appendix.
Slow. Example: bradycardia, an abnormally slow heart rate.
Above normal or excessive. Example: hypertension, high blood pressure.
Below normal or deficient. Example: hypoglycemia, low blood sugar.
Bad, difficult, or painful. Example: dyspnea, difficult breathing.
Without or absence of. Example: apnea, a temporary stop in breathing.
Around. Example: pericardium, the sac surrounding the heart.
Within or inside. Example: intravenous, within a vein.
Many or excessive. Example: polyuria, producing an excessive amount of urine.
Half. Example: hemiplegia, paralysis of one side of the body.
Study of. Example: cardiology, the study of the heart.
Pain. Example: neuralgia, nerve pain.
Cutting into; incision. Example: tracheotomy, an incision into the trachea.
Surgical creation of an opening. Example: colostomy, an opening from the colon through the abdominal wall.
Visual examination with an instrument. Example: endoscopy, viewing inside the body with a scope.
Surgical repair or reshaping. Example: rhinoplasty, surgery to reshape the nose.
Condition of the blood. Example: anemia, a shortage of red blood cells or hemoglobin.
Deficiency. Example: leukopenia, a low white blood cell count.
Tumor or mass. Example: lipoma, a benign tumor made of fat tissue.
Disease. Example: neuropathy, disease or damage of the nerves.
Enlargement. Example: cardiomegaly, an enlarged heart.
Flow or discharge. Example: rhinorrhea, a runny nose.
